sourceFacts.fact: In Duchenne muscular dystrophy, hip extensor weakness contributes to increased lumbar lordosis and posterior trunk compensation.
This is a compensatory movement association; the diagram should not claim a measured force model or specify internal muscle anatomy.

clinicalSources.title: Sutherland et al: The pathomechanics of gait in Duchenne muscular dystrophy

layoutSpecification: Title 'A compensation for hip weakness'. Three-stage left-to-right conceptual movement diagram. LEFT: a simple low-strength gauge labelled 'Hip extensors weak'. CENTRE: one fully clothed neutral child seen in simple side profile, facing RIGHT, feet on floor, knees gently straight, torso modestly leaning backward; a small curved arrow beside shoulders points BACK toward viewer's LEFT, label 'Trunk leans back'. RIGHT: an isolated abstract CURVED RIBBON shaped like a gentle inward lumbar curve, clearly disconnected from any body and labelled 'Lumbar lordosis increases'. It is a shape mnemonic, not a spine drawing. Connect stages with teal rightward cause-association arrows. No exposed muscles, pelvis, vertebrae, gravity line, force vectors through joints or mathematical angles. Do not exaggerate child pose into a fall. Small bottom 'Movement concept • no force measurements'.
forbiddenAnatomy: No internal organ, eye, ear, brain, tissue or bone anatomy
No diagnostic image, patient-specific lesion appearance or literal anatomical pathway
